Agrix Technical Deep-Dive Curriculum

Targeted interview notes, architecture diagrams, and production code patterns.

When interviewing for Agrix's web platform, emphasize that building an agricultural portal is fundamentally different from a typical SaaS dashboard. Farmers, supply chain operators, and warehouse managers frequently operate in rural areas with poor 3G/4G connectivity and bright outdoor sunlight.

Key Technical Themes to Highlight:
  • Offline-First & Optimistic Updates: Using TanStack React Query with indexedDB persistence so inventory counts can be checked in warehouses with no signal.
  • Custom Telemetry Hooks: Implementing useTelemetryStream(sensorId) with automatic reconnection and exponential backoff.
  • List Virtualization: Rendering tens of thousands of stock-keeping units (SKUs) of produce without browser freezing using @tanstack/react-virtual.
  • High-Contrast UI: Tailwind CSS color tokens designed for outdoor glare visibility.
// Production Custom Hook: IoT Cold-Chain Polling
function useColdChainTelemetry(siloId) {
  const [data, setData] = useState(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    let active = true;
    const poll = async () => {
      try {
        const res = await fetch(`/api/v1/silos/${siloId}/metrics`);
        const json = await res.json();
        if (active) setData(json);
      } catch(err) { console.error(err); }
    };
    const timer = setInterval(poll, 5000);
    return () => { active = false; clearInterval(timer); };
  }, [siloId]);
  return data;
}

Why did Agrix choose FastAPI over Django or Flask? You must be able to articulate: (1) Native ASGI asynchronous execution for high-throughput I/O with IoT temperature monitors; (2) Automatic Swagger / OpenAPI generation for rapid frontend contract alignment; (3) Pydantic's C-compiled validation speed in v2.

# Production FastAPI Endpoint with Background Task & Pydantic Validation
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks, Depends, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List

class CropIngestionBatch(BaseModel):
  crop_id: str
  quantity_kg: float = Field(..., gt=0)
  harvest_date: str
  ambient_temp_c: float

@app.post("/api/v1/inventory/intake", status_code=202)
async def ingest_crop_batch(batch: CropIngestionBatch, bg: BackgroundTasks):
  # Non-blocking async persistence + queue ML decay estimation
  record_id = await db_inventory.insert(batch.model_dump())
  bg.add_task(run_ml_spoilage_prediction, record_id, batch.ambient_temp_c)
  return {"status": "queued", "batch_id": record_id}

Standard retail inventory models (like basic EOQ or static min/max thresholds) catastrophically fail in agriculture. Crops are biological assets with non-linear shelf life decay governed by temperature and humidity kinetics (Arrhenius equation).

1. Demand Forecasting Features:

Models like LightGBM or Prophet trained on:

  • Wholesale Mandi market price trends
  • Regional festival & holiday demand spikes
  • Local weather forecasts (rainfall affects harvest)
  • Historical weekly seasonality
2. FEFO Dispatching vs FIFO:

First-In-First-Out (FIFO) causes high waste because batches arriving earlier might have been harvested later or stored better.

Dispatch Priority Score = (Remaining Days to Spoilage) / (Transit Time to Destination Retailer)

In the Agrix system design round, draw this 4-tier architecture:

[Client Tier]: React SPA (Tailwind + PWA Service Worker for Offline Warehouse Scanning)
    │ (HTTPS REST + WebSocket telemetry alerts)
[API Gateway]: FastAPI (Uvicorn ASGI workers, OAuth2 JWT auth, rate limiting)
    │ (Task Queue / Fast Cache)
[Caching & Queue]: Redis (Session cache, real-time alert pub/sub, Celery broker)
    │ (Async Engine)
[ML & Database]: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB (sensor hyper-tables) + ONNX Runtime for ML inference

🔌 Part 1: The ECE-to-Software Mental Translator

Whenever a software term sounds intimidating, map it to the hardware/circuit equivalent you already studied in ECE:

React.js Component ECE: IC Chip (e.g., 74HC00 / 555 Timer)

Just like you build a complex PCB by snapping together reusable IC chips instead of wiring individual transistors, a React website is built from reusable UI blocks called Components (like a <CropCard /> or <Navbar />).

Props vs. State in React ECE: Input Pins vs. Flip-Flop Register

Props are external input signals fed into an IC's pins from outside (read-only). State (`useState`) is like an internal D Flip-Flop memory register inside the chip—when its stored value changes, the display refreshes automatically!

FastAPI & REST JSON ECE: UART / SPI / I2C Bus

How does an Arduino talk to a sensor? Over a serial protocol like UART or I2C using data packets. In web apps, the React browser talks to the Python FastAPI server over HTTP using text packets called JSON.

Async / Await in FastAPI ECE: Hardware Interrupts (ISR)

In microcontrollers, polling blocks the CPU while waiting for a slow sensor. Interrupts let the CPU do other work until the data is ready. In FastAPI, async/await works just like an interrupt so the server can handle 1,000 warehouse sensors at once!

Pydantic Validation ECE: Signal Conditioning / Bandpass Filter

Before feeding a noisy analog signal into an ADC, you pass it through a filter and voltage clamp so it doesn't fry the circuit. Pydantic is FastAPI's input filter—it rejects corrupted or negative crop weights before they touch your database.

Agri-ML Spoilage & FEFO ECE: Exponential RC Decay & DHT22 Sensors

Crop freshness decays exponentially with temperature just like an RC circuit discharge or thermal semiconductor curve (Arrhenius law). Using IoT temperature/humidity logs (like DHT22 sensors), our ML model predicts remaining shelf life and ships the oldest batch first (FEFO).

🎙️ How to Pitch Your ECE Background in the Interview

Word-for-Word Scripts

Many ECE students worry about competing with CS students. At an AgriTech company like Agrix, your ECE background is actually a huge advantage because warehouse inventory relies on physical IoT temperature/humidity sensors! Memorize these 3 answers:

Q1: "You're from B.Tech ECE. Why apply for Software & ML at Agrix?"

"In ECE, I learned how physical sensors capture temperature, humidity, and telemetry data, and how signals behave over time. At Agrix, optimizing agricultural inventory isn't just pure abstract software—it's about taking noisy real-world cold-storage sensor streams, exposing them cleanly through FastAPI & React dashboards, and applying Machine Learning to prevent crop spoilage. My ECE foundation lets me understand both the physical sensor behavior and the software/ML pipeline."

Q2: "Walk me through the Agrix internship role on your profile."

"The role has two connected phases. Phase 1 focuses on building Agrix's responsive web platform using React.js on the frontend and Python FastAPI on the backend so farmers and warehouse managers can track stock in real time, even on mobile networks. Phase 2 transitions into Machine Learning—using historical demand and storage temperature logs to predict crop shelf-life decay, automate FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) dispatch, and calculate optimal reorder points."

Q3: "What happens if an IoT warehouse sensor sends a glitchy reading like -999°C?"

"Just like we use signal conditioning filters in ECE before an ADC, I use Pydantic schema validation in FastAPI (`Field(ge=-10, le=50)`) to immediately reject out-of-range spikes at the API boundary, and in the ML pipeline I use rolling median imputation so a single faulty thermistor packet doesn't corrupt our spoilage forecast."

🔍 Beginner Cheat Sheet: All 4 Coding Sandbox Solutions Explained

Don't know Python syntax well yet? Here is the plain-English formula behind all 4 coding challenges in the Live Coding Sandbox tab:

1. Dynamic Reorder Point (`calculate_reorder_level`)

Idea: Order more stock before you run out during delivery (`lead_time_days`), plus a safety buffer, inflated to cover daily crop rot (`spoilage_rate`).

base = daily_demand * lead_time_days
safety = safety_factor * daily_demand * math.sqrt(lead_time_days)
return round((base + safety) / (1 - spoilage_rate))
2. Arrhenius Thermal Decay (`predict_remaining_days`)

Idea: Every 10°C above ideal cold storage (4°C) doubles the speed of rotting (`2 ** ((temp - 4) / 10)`). Humidity above 85% adds extra penalty.

temp_factor = 2 ** ((current_temp_c - 4.0) / 10.0)
hum_factor = 1 + max(0, (humidity_pct - 85) * 0.015)
return round(base_shelf_life_days / (temp_factor * hum_factor), 2)
3. FEFO Warehouse Batch Dispatcher (`allocate_fefo_batches`)

Idea: Filter out expired batches (`remaining_days <= 0`), sort remaining batches by lowest `remaining_days` first (`key=lambda b: b['remaining_days']`), and greedily take quantity until the order is filled.

4. LLM Hallucination & Faithfulness Scorer (`score_response_quality`)

Idea: Check if forbidden safety strings appear in the response (`0.0` if unsafe), then count what fraction of `required_facts` appear in the lowercase answer.
